title: Spying & Privacy in Islam
subtitle: Islamic guidance on digital spying, privacy, permission, trust, and protecting the dignity of others.

cards.title: What Counts as Digital Spying?
cards.paragraph: Digital spying means deliberately searching for someone’s private information without permission or a legitimate reason.

cards.title: Do Not Spy
cards.paragraph: The Qur’an teaches: “Wa la tajassasu” — do not spy. Suspicion should not become an invasion of another person’s privacy.

cards.title: Respect Permission
cards.paragraph: Private messages, phones, photos, and conversations should not be opened, copied, recorded, or shared without permission.

cards.title: Protect Digital Trust
cards.paragraph: Protecting private information strengthens trust, dignity, friendships, families, and responsible online communication.

floatingText.title: Digital Spying
floatingText.paragraph: Curiosity does not create permission to enter someone’s private life.

floatingText.title: Do Not Spy
floatingText.paragraph: Avoid suspicion before it turns into searching and invading privacy.

floatingText.title: Ask Permission
floatingText.paragraph: Silence should never automatically be treated as consent.

floatingText.title: Protect Trust
floatingText.paragraph: Guard private information even when nobody else is watching.
